question: Is 2017 East 17th Street, Brooklyn in any of the DEP stormwater flood scenarios?

plan.rationale: The query specifies a precise street address in Brooklyn, requiring geocoding to a single locatable point to assess its inclusion in DEP stormwater flood scenarios.

claims.text: This address is mapped within FEMA flood zone X, per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970352F, effective 2007.
No Hurricane Ida high-water marks were surveyed within 800 meters of this address; the nearest USGS-surveyed mark is 1351 meters away.
Experimental: satellite-detected surface water about 14 hours after Hurricane Ida showed no water polygons within 500 meters of this address; the nearest water polygon is 2401.9 meters away.
Within 800 meters of this address, there are 5 MTA subway entrances: 0 are inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 3 are inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise).
Within 1500 meters of this address, there is 1 NYC DOE school: 0 are inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 1 is inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise).
Within 3000 meters of this address, there are 3 hospitals: 1 is inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 2 are inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise).
Experimental: a TTM model forecasts a peak surge residual of 0.53 meters at The Battery about 9 hours ahead.
Experimental: the TTM forecast projects about 0.11 flood-related 311 complaints within 200 meters over the next 96 days.
NPCC4 projects a sea-level rise of 0.38 meters (15 inches) by the 2050s and 0.79 meters (31 inches) by 2100 at the Battery, relative to 2000-2004; the 90th percentile is 0.74 meters and 1.65 meters.
Hurricane Sandy devastated New York City in October 2012, covering large swaths of the five boroughs, including many NYCHA campuses, with salt water and debris.
This stretch of 4 Avenue Brooklyn in the Gowanus neighborhood is prone to chronic flooding and has been impacted by heavy rainfall at five stations.
